nodes.label: Frozen HMAC timestamp on a client built once outside the poll loop
nodes.norm_label: frozen hmac timestamp on a client built once outside the poll loop

nodes.label: send_normal_text built a bare Client::builder() with no proxy auth headers, so it always 401s against the proxy
nodes.norm_label: bare client without proxy auth always 401s

nodes.label: download_file called bytes() for any HTTP status, storing a proxy 401 or Telegram 404 error body as photo bytes
nodes.norm_label: download file stores error body as image bytes

nodes.label: Message had no document field and Update had no edited_message, so serde dropped them while the offset was already persisted and the update was acknowledged and lost forever
nodes.norm_label: serde drops unparsed updates before offset persist

nodes.label: Telegram gives no guarantee that the last entry of a photo array is the largest, so the largest is picked by width times height
nodes.norm_label: telegram photo array order is not a size guarantee

nodes.label: send_photo hardcodes filename image.png and MIME image/png regardless of the real bytes
nodes.norm_label: send photo hardcodes png filename and mime

nodes.label: Browser sniffing overrides the declared image MIME subtype
nodes.norm_label: browser sniffing overrides declared image mime subtype

nodes.label: Rebuild the client inside the loop instead of mutating an existing one, because build_client installs the timestamp as a default header at construction so only a fresh client carries a current signature
nodes.norm_label: rebuild client in loop because default headers are set at construction

nodes.label: Extracted the download_file status check into an ensure_success helper because a network test was impractical and tests must not make HTTP calls
nodes.norm_label: extract status guard into testable helper to avoid network in tests

nodes.label: Offset ordering was deliberately left unchanged because moving the persist after the message guard would change acknowledgement semantics and risk redelivery loops
nodes.norm_label: offset persist ordering left alone to avoid redelivery loops

nodes.label: NUT hardware-compatibility support level used as a UPS buying criterion
nodes.norm_label: nut hardware compatibility support level used as ups buying criterion

nodes.label: UPower's NUT-generated HID UPS backend races NUT inside KDE Plasma
nodes.norm_label: upower nut generated hid ups backend races nut in kde plasma

nodes.label: nut-monitor.service is a historic misnomer: the upstream unit runs upsmon, not the NUT-Monitor Python GUI client
nodes.norm_label: nut monitor service runs upsmon not the gui

nodes.label: The modified-sine-wave-destroys-your-PSU claim is a vendor risk-mitigation narrative, with no defect bulletin, teardown, or reproducible test behind it; the documented failure is the PC shutting itself off on transfer
nodes.norm_label: modified sine psu damage is a vendor narrative not a documented failure

nodes.label: The ATX 17 ms hold-up figure is specified at 100% of rated load, so a 100 W system on a 500 W PSU has several times that margin and a 10 ms UPS transfer is not the problem
nodes.norm_label: atx 17 ms hold up is a full load figure

nodes.label: A plain UPS is not ACPI-aware and exposes no _AC/_AT adapter object, so acpid cannot detect mains loss through it on a desktop
nodes.norm_label: acpi has no ac adapter object for a desktop ups

nodes.label: A smart plug deliberately left on mains outside the UPS, polled over HTTP by a systemd service and timer, is the working substitute when the UPS has no comms port
nodes.norm_label: dedicated smart plug on mains as an outage probe

nodes.label: 2023-2024 APC BX****MI firmware reports phantom LB and RB at full charge, risking a false shutdown; fixed by NUT PR 2565, released in 2.8.3
nodes.norm_label: apc bx series firmware phantom low battery

nodes.label: Plasma's own on-battery profile must be set to No Action because otherwise it races NUT and can suspend the machine in the middle of the shutdown
nodes.norm_label: plasma on battery profile set to no action so nut owns shutdown

nodes.label: NUT was chosen because it is the only daemon covering APC, CyberPower and Eaton together, apcupsd being APC-only and PowerPanel brand-locked
nodes.norm_label: nut chosen because it alone covers all four brands

nodes.label: Pure sine wave exists at 1000-1500 VA from CyberPower for roughly the price of a 650 VA stepped-sine unit, which makes it cheap insurance for an APFC PSU
nodes.norm_label: pure sine at 1000 va is cheap insurance for an apfc psu

nodes.label: Transfer time is not the risk because hold-up scales with capacitor energy over power, so at a fifth of rated load the margin is 3-5x; the real risk is hold-up degradation from aged bulk capacitors, and the waveform is a separate smaller risk
nodes.norm_label: transfer time is not the problem waveform is
